mastered.detail: Learned. One quick round in a week or two keeps it.

practising.label: Almost there
practising.detail: Nearly learned. The best place to spend the next session.

learning.label: Just started
learning.detail: Too soon to tell how it is going. A few more rounds will show.

struggling.label: Needs help
struggling.detail: More wrong than right. Start here.

not-started.label: Not tried
not-started.detail: Has not played this one yet.

off_by_one.label: Off by one
off_by_one.detail: Lands next to the right answer — the idea is there, the count slips at the end.
off_by_one.fix: Count out loud together and touch each thing once. The last word said is the answer.

off_by_more.label: Not close
off_by_more.detail: The answer is far from the target, which usually means the method was not used.
off_by_more.fix: Drop to smaller numbers for a round or two, until the method is being used again.

reversed.label: The wrong way round
reversed.detail: Right numbers, wrong direction — comparing or ordering the opposite way.
reversed.fix: Say it as a sentence before answering: “six is more than four”.

guessed_fast.label: Guessing
guessed_fast.detail: Answering faster than the thinking takes. Often boredom, sometimes avoidance.
guessed_fast.fix: Ask them to say the answer out loud before they tap it.

timed_out.label: Ran out of time
timed_out.detail: No answer given. Worth watching whether the question is hard or just long.
timed_out.fix: Sit alongside for one round and see where the pause comes.

miscounted_items.label: Lost count
miscounted_items.detail: Counted more or fewer things than were there — one-to-one matching is not secure yet.
miscounted_items.fix: Move each thing aside as it is counted, so nothing is counted twice or missed.

sequence_slip.label: Broke the pattern
sequence_slip.detail: Wrong next term in a sequence: the rule, rather than the arithmetic.
sequence_slip.fix: Say the run aloud from the start — 2, 4, 6 — and ask what comes next.

place_value.label: Tens and ones
place_value.detail: Reading tens and ones the wrong way round — 15 for 51, or 3 tens read as 3.
place_value.fix: Build the number with ten-sticks and single ones before writing it down.

unknown.label: Not classified

start.label: Often starts a stroke in the wrong place
start.fix: let them watch the stroke once more, then put the pencil on the green dot before starting

direction.label: Often draws strokes the wrong way
direction.fix: trace the stroke in the air together, following the arrow, before writing it

order.label: Often writes the strokes out of order
order.fix: say the numbers out loud together — one, two, three — as they write

checkpoint.label: Often skips part of a curve or loop
checkpoint.fix: slow down at the curls; ask them to touch each star on the path

coverage.label: Often stops a stroke too early
coverage.fix: ask them to keep going until they reach the end of the path

path.label: Writing is wobbly
path.fix: use Strokes on for a few more tries, and go slowly

scribble.label: Writes very fast
scribble.fix: praise slow, careful strokes more than finishing quickly

placement.label: Puts vowels on the wrong side of the letter
placement.fix: say where the vowel sits — before, after, above or below — before they write

missing.label: Leaves out a stroke
missing.fix: count the strokes together before writing

unfit.label: Stops after a little writing
unfit.fix: sit with them for the first try and encourage the whole letter

traceStudio.title: Trace Studio
traceStudio.subtitle: Build letters and drawings for children to trace, then group them into collections.
traceStudio.empty: No items yet. Start a new one, or copy an example.

modeHint.adjust: Drag a stroke to move it, or drag its points and handles. ⌥/Alt-drag the curve to bend it. The box around the selected stroke resizes it (Shift keeps its shape). Drag a stroke’s number to move the number. Arrow keys nudge a point, or the whole stroke when no point is selected; Shift moves 10. Shift+click adds strokes to the selection; ⌘G groups them, ⇧⌘G ungroups.
modeHint.add: Click on the selected stroke to add a point there. Click empty space to extend it.
modeHint.pen: Draw a stroke with your finger or mouse. It becomes smooth, editable points. A tap makes a dot.
modeHint.pin: Click on the selected stroke to pin a checkpoint the child must pass. Click a pinned one to remove it.
modeHint.hand: Drag to move around a zoomed canvas. Hold Space to pan with any tool; Ctrl or ⌘ + scroll zooms.
modeHint.cut: Click a stroke where one stroke should end and the next begin. Each piece gets its own number.

traceStudio.noStrokes: No strokes yet. Draw one with the pen, or add a shape.
traceStudio.loopLeft: Add a loop, curling left (at the chosen point, or the end)
traceStudio.loopRight: Add a loop, curling right (at the chosen point, or the end)
traceStudio.guideNote: What you trace over. The child never sees it; they see the strokes.
traceStudio.writingNote: Writing: the stroke order must be right, and a child earns “can write” from memory.
traceStudio.drawingNote: Drawing: any stroke order is fine, and a child earns “can draw” at the faded step.
traceStudio.stepsNote: Choose the steps a child climbs and the score each needs. The last step earns the tick. Test-write every step before publishing.
traceStudio.pickStepToTest: Pick a step and press Test to write it the way a child will.

check.insideCanvas: Every point is inside the canvas
check.continueTouches: Strokes that carry on really touch
check.planEndsAtCanDo: The steps end with the tick

traceStudio.allChecksPass: Everything passes. Publishing arrives in the next phase.

traceStudio.selectHint: Select a stroke on the canvas or in the list to edit it.
traceStudio.badgeHint: Drag a stroke’s number to move it.
traceStudio.shapesNote: Pick a shape. It becomes a stroke you can edit like any other.
traceStudio.glyphPlaceholder: Type a letter to trace over
traceStudio.multiHint: Drag any of them to move them together; the box around them resizes them all. Each stroke keeps its own number.
